title: Connected monodromy torsor trivializing a finite locally constant sheaf of sets
statement: Let U be a nonempty connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme] and F a finite locally constant sheaf of sets on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. There are a finite group Q in Type u and a connected finite etale ULift(Q)-torsor c:Y -> U [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois] such that the set inverse image c^{-1}F is constant [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Empty F is allowed.

proof.text: Choose a geometric point and apply the finite-etale/FLC equivalence and the fundamental-group equivalence to obtain a finite discrete continuous fundamental-group set S.

The image Q in the permutation group of S is finite. The kernel is the intersection of the finitely many open stabilizers, hence open and normal. Shrink Q to the universe of U. The regular transitive Q-set gives a connected finite etale cover. Its commuting right translations, converted to a left action by inversion, make it a Q-torsor; transport the action along Q equivalent to ULift Q.

The fundamental group of the cover acts on S through the kernel. Pullback compatibility therefore identifies the inverse image of F with a constant sheaf. For empty S the image group is trivial and the cover is the identity.

proof_origin.note: Finite monodromy set image and explicit universe/action transport.
